correctness.rationale: The generating function F(q)=product_{v=a,b,c}(1-q^v)^{-1} has a triple pole at q=1. Because gcd(a,b,c)=1, every nonidentity pole has order <=2 and double poles arise exactly at common nontrivial roots of pair denominations. The three pair-gcds are mutually coprime, avoiding overlapping double-pole classes. Taking coefficients and the finite Fourier sawtooth yields Delta(n)=n/(abc)[1+sum_{pairs} t(-u+d*epsilon(n))]+O(1) with bounded L-periodic remainder. CRT makes all nonwrap and wrap epsilon statuses simultaneous and yields strictly negative (when all v>=2) and positive leading slopes on positive-density classes. For exactly one shared pair, signs exhaust classes and densities are (d-u)/d and u/d, no ties eventually. The a=1 boundary reduces Delta to a two-generator denumerant, giving nonnegative values and eventual 1/gcd(b,c) positive density. I independently checked exact first-difference quasipolynomial slopes across all residues for eight primitive families by dynamic counting, not as an infinite proof. Includes repeated denominations if overall gcd=1; stabilizing index is not quantified.
